findings.note: The @TODO@ placeholder does not evade the lint it is meant to evade. lintscope_test.go:8-12 claims the markers are 'assembled at run time and written as placeholders ... so that this file does not trip the very lints it tests', but todoPattern (internal/reviewers/taskdone.go:93) is (?i)\b(TODO|FIXME)\b and '@' is a non-word character, so '@TODO@' matches. lintscope_test.go is a .go file and therefore lintable() == true, so all eight added lines carrying '@TODO@' (lines 19, 30, 32, 37, 64, 82, 140, 213) reach the lints. I confirmed end to end by running RunTaskDone over the real base..head diff of this file: it emits the high finding 'TODO left in task-done diff' with Found = 'return strings.ReplaceAll(diff, "@TODO@", todoWord)'. Per the task-done rubric ('The diff adds TODO or FIXME markers') this blocks. Fix: assemble the placeholder too (e.g. "@"+"TO"+"DO"+"@") or rename it to a token that contains neither word, e.g. @MARKER@.

findings.note: The same self-tripping problem, worse, for the eval lint. lintscope_test.go:31 contains the fixture prose line '+The winning pair comes from the judge-eval (§17), not gpt-5.2.' Inside the test that line is docs prose and is correctly excluded, but the line as it appears in this branch's own diff of lintscope_test.go (a .go file) matches evalPattern \beval\s*\( -- the hyphen before 'eval' is a word boundary and ' (' satisfies \s*\(. Running RunTaskDone over the real base..head diff of this file emits 'critical Unsafe eval introduced' with Found = 'The winning pair comes from the judge-eval (§17), not gpt-5.2.' So the branch that adds the docs-exclusion fix cannot pass its own eval gate on account of this file. Fix: reword to remove the space before the paren (e.g. 'judge-eval(§17)' would still match; use 'judge eval, §17') or route it through the @EVAL@-style placeholder, which does not match.
